title_en: Guangzhou Hailongwang Investment Development Co., Ltd. v. Guangzhou Municipal Commission of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, Guangdong Province — dispute over administrative decision
keywords_en: Administrative; Dispute over administrative disposition decision; First instance; High People's Court; Guangdong Province; Legal person; State organ; Administrative Procedure Law; Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Venture Law; Plaintiff qualification; Justiciability of internal administrative acts; Legality of administrative disposition decision; Approval of foreign-invested projects; Revocation of administrative reply; Cooperative real estate development; Dispute over administrative disposition decision of the Economic and Trade Committee
full_text_en:
**Guangzhou Hailongwang Investment Development Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Province Guangzhou**
**Foreign Economic and Trade Commission — Dispute over Administrative Decision**

**Plaintiff:** Guangzhou Hailongwang Investment Development Co., Ltd. Address: Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
**Legal Representative:** Liang Hande, Chairman of the Board.
**Agents ad litem:** Zhang Zhenya and Lyu Hui, lawyers from Guangdong Zhengping Tiancheng Law Firm.

**Defendant:** Guangdong Province Guangzhou Foreign Economic and Trade Commission.
**Legal Representative:** Jiang Houxi, Director of the Commission.
**Agents ad litem:** He Yanfei, lawyer from Guangzhou Jinqiao Law Firm; Hou Jinbing, lawyer from Guangzhou Jinglun Law Firm.

**Third Party:** Guangdong Province Guangzhou Municipal People's Government Overseas Chinese Affairs Office.
**Legal Representative:** Xu Guanghan, Director of the Office.
**Agents ad litem:** Ye Dongwen, lawyer from Guangzhou Jinglun Law Firm; Yao Baohui, cadre of the Guangdong Province Guangzhou Municipal People's Government Overseas Chinese Affairs Office.

**Third Party:** Guangzhou Sanlian Overseas Chinese Real Estate Co., Ltd. Address: Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
**Legal Representative:** Ye Jianxun, Chairman of the Board.
**Agents ad litem:** Liang Jinhao, staff member of Guangzhou Sanlian Overseas Chinese Real Estate Co., Ltd.; Wei Yanru, lawyer from Guangzhou Jinglun Law Firm.

**Third Party:** Guangdong Pearl River Investment Co., Ltd. Address: Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
**Legal Representative:** He Guohua, Chairman of the Board.
**Agents ad litem:** Jiang Ping, Professor at China University of Political Science and Law; Qiu Haiyang, Doctoral candidate at China University of Political Science and Law.

**Third Party:** Guangzhou Pearl River Qiaodu Real Estate Co., Ltd. Address: Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
**Legal Representative:** Liang Jinhao, Chairman of the Board.
**Agents ad litem:** Liu Heng, lawyer from Guangdong Lingnan Law Firm; Tan Ning, staff member of Guangzhou Pearl River Qiaodu Real Estate Co., Ltd.

**Third Party:** British Virgin Islands Guangda Investment Co., Ltd. Address: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
**Legal Representative:** Xie Shidong, Director of the Company.
**Agents ad litem:** Mao Hewen, staff member of British Virgin Islands Guangda Investment Co., Ltd.; Liao Yanming, lawyer from Guangdong Haiyin Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Guangzhou Hailongwang Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hailongwang Company), refused to accept the administrative decision rendered by the Guangdong Province Guangzhou Foreign Economic and Trade Commission (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission) on October 25, 1999, in the form of the Document Suiwai Jingmaoye [1999] No. 233, "Notice on Revoking the Document Suiwai Jingmaoye [1999] No. 143 of Our Commission" (hereinafter referred to as Notice No. 233), and filed a lawsuit with the Guangdong High People's Court.

Since the Notice No. 233 made by the defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission directly involved the Guangzhou Municipal People's Government Overseas Chinese Affairs Office (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office), Guangzhou Sanlian Overseas Chinese Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanlian Company), Guangdong Pearl River Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pearl River Company), Guangzhou Pearl River Qiaodu Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qiaodu Company), British Virgin Islands Guangda Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangda Company), and other relevant departments and enterprises, the Guangdong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 27 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, notified the above departments and enterprises to participate in the lawsuit as third parties in this case.

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** The Notice No. 233 made by the defendant, which revoked the previously issued Document Suiwai Jingmaoye [1999] No. 143, "Notice on Revolving Three Approval Documents of Our Commission" (hereinafter referred to as Notice No. 143) merely on the basis of "upon deliberation," constitutes an illegal specific administrative act and should be revoked. The defendant's initial approval of the establishment of Qiaodu Company violated relevant legal provisions, and the decision in Notice No. 143 to revoke Qiaodu Company was correct. Based on the agreement with Sanlian Company, our company invested 50% in the Guangzhou Qiaodu project and holds a 50% development right in that project. The defendant's revocation of Notice No. 143 has left our company's actual investment unprotected by law and rendered us unable to benefit from the actual investment. We request the revocation of the defendant's Notice No. 233 and seek reimbursement of litigation costs.

**Defendant's Defense:** The Notice No. 143 issued by our commission in 1999 within our authority contained errors in the application of law. Therefore, pursuant to Article 5 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Ventures and Articles 3 and 5 of the Regulations of Guangzhou Municipality on the Administration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises, we issued Notice No. 233 to correct it. Notice No. 233 was addressed to the Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office and constitutes an internal administrative act. This administrative act does not infringe upon the plaintiff's property rights, and the plaintiff has no right to bring a lawsuit. The agreement between the plaintiff and Sanlian Company pertains to a separate legal relationship and is unrelated to Notice No. 233.

**Defense of Third Party, Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office:** Our office is the supervising authority for Sanlian Company, the Chinese partner of Qiaodu Company. Documents concerning the establishment and modification of Qiaodu Company must be submitted by our office to the defendant for approval. Notice No. 233 is an internal administrative act issued by the defendant to our office, and the plaintiff is not the counterparty to this administrative act. The lawful investors and shareholders of the Pearl River Qiaodu project are Sanlian Company, Pearl River Company, and Guangda Company. The plaintiff is neither an investor nor entitled to any investment rights or interests. The Notice No. 233 issued by the defendant did not infringe upon the plaintiff's property rights. As the plaintiff has no legal interest in this administrative act, it lacks standing as a plaintiff. We request the dismissal of the plaintiff's lawsuit.

**Defense of Third Party, Sanlian Company:** Neither the defendant's Notice No. 233 nor Notice No. 143 has any administrative legal relationship with the plaintiff, nor do they infringe upon the plaintiff's property rights. The RMB 60 million paid by the plaintiff to our company in December 1998 constitutes a creditor-debtor relationship between our company and the plaintiff, which is unrelated to Notice No. 233. We request the dismissal of the plaintiff's lawsuit.

**Defense of Third Party, Pearl River Company:** Neither Notice No. 143 nor Notice No. 233 was directed at the plaintiff, and the plaintiff does not satisfy the conditions for filing an administrative lawsuit. While Notice No. 233, in correcting Notice No. 143, did not specify the facts or cite specific laws, this does not mean the specific administrative act itself lacks a basis. We request the dismissal of the plaintiff's lawsuit.

**Defense of Third Party, Qiaodu Company:** The specific administrative act under suit did not harm the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests. The plaintiff is not a shareholder of Qiaodu Company, and the investment dispute between the plaintiff and Sanlian Company is a separate legal relationship that should be resolved through civil procedure and is unrelated to the administrative act under suit. We request the dismissal of the plaintiff's claims.

**Defense of Third Party, Guangda Company:** The plaintiff has no direct interest in the specific administrative act under suit and does not meet the conditions for filing an administrative lawsuit. The defendant's initial Notice No. 143 revoking Qiaodu Company directly harmed the lawful rights and interests of Qiaodu Company and its shareholders and was clearly erroneous. Correcting this error was not improper, and the plaintiff's grounds for the lawsuit are untenable. We request the dismissal of the plaintiff's claims.

The main evidence submitted by the parties to the court includes: Approval No. 337, Approval No. 6, and Approval No. 9 issued by the Guangzhou Foreign Economic and Trade Commission; the "Contract for Cooperative Development and Operation of Pearl River Qiaodu Real Estate" and its articles of association signed by Sanlian Company, Pearl River Company, and Guangda Company; the agreement signed between Sanlian Company and Hailongwang Company; the "Resolution of the Standing Committee of the Guangzhou Municipal People's Congress on Deliberating the Implementation Plan Proposed by the Municipal People's Government for the No. 42 Motion of the Third Session of the Ninth Municipal People's Congress"; the "Meeting Minutes" of the Pearl River Qiaodu Preparatory Committee; and Notice No. 143 and Notice No. 233 issued by the Guangzhou Foreign Economic and Trade Commission.

**Facts Found by the Guangdong High People's Court upon Trial:**

The Pearl River Qiaodu project is a key construction project in Guangzhou's urban development. The Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office is the administrative department in charge of this project, and the Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission is the administrative authority responsible for the examination and approval of Sino-foreign cooperative joint ventures and their supervision. Pursuant to relevant resolutions of the Standing Committee of the Guangzhou Municipal People's Congress, a special Preparatory Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Preparatory Committee) was established for the Pearl River Qiaodu project, responsible for reviewing the planning and design of the project, and guiding and coordinating major issues such as land acquisition and investment. On October 27, 1997, the defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission issued Suiwai Jingmaoye [1997] No. 337, "Approval on the Supplementary Contract and Supplementary Articles of Association for the Cooperative Operation of Guangzhou Qiaofeng Real Estate Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as Approval No. 337), approving the "Equity Transfer Agreement" and the "Supplementary Contract to the Contract for Cooperative Development and Operation of 'Pearl River Qiaodu' Real Estate" and its supplementary articles of association signed by Hong Kong Jiayu Company and British Virgin Islands Aiguang Property Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aiguang Company) on the 17th of the same month, and agreeing that Sanlian Company and Aiguang Company would jointly develop the Pearl River Qiaodu project. On January 12, 1998, the defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission issued Suiwai Jingmaoye [1998] No. 6, "Approval on the Early Termination of the Contract and Articles of Association of the Cooperative Operation of Guangzhou Qiaofeng Real Estate Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as Approval No. 6), approving the "Agreement on Termination of the Contract for Cooperative Development and Operation of Pearl River Qiaodu Real Estate" signed by Sanlian Company and Aiguang Company on the 8th of the same month, agreeing to the early termination of the contract and articles of association of the cooperative enterprise Guangzhou Qiaofeng Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qiaofeng Company), the dissolution of that cooperative company, and the return of the project's approval certificate. On January 15 of the same year, the defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission issued Approval No. 9, approving the establishment of the Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise Qiaodu Company by Sanlian Company, Pearl River Company, and Guangda Company, and approving the "Contract for Cooperative Development and Operation of Pearl River Qiaodu Real Estate" and its articles of association signed by the three companies on the 12th of the same month, agreeing that the cooperative enterprise Qiaodu Company would develop the Pearl River Qiaodu project, and approving the investment ratios and profit-sharing ratios of the cooperative parties.

On December 28, 1998, Sanlian Company, which participated in the investment of the Pearl River Qiaodu project, signed an "Agreement" with Hailongwang Company stipulating: Hailongwang Company, as a joint investor in the Pearl River Qiaodu project, would pay RMB 60 million, which would also serve as an advance payment for acquiring a 50% investment and development right in the entire project; after receiving this payment, Sanlian Company would, in accordance with the directives of the leaders of the Guangzhou Pearl River Qiaodu Construction Preparatory Committee, organize negotiations among relevant parties, implement matters such as securing Hailongwang Company's 50% development right in the Pearl River Qiaodu project, and protect Hailongwang Company's rights and interests; if the cooperation was established, Hailongwang Company's advance payment could be converted into registered capital of a new project company established with its participation; if the cooperation was not established, Sanlian Company would return the payment with interest within one month; if Sanlian Company failed to return it on time, Hailongwang Company could require Sanlian Company to repay the amount using land use rights valued at RMB 500,000 per mu, meaning Sanlian Company should then repay Hailongwang Company's investment of RMB 60 million with 120 mu of land use rights, and be responsible for transferring those land use rights to Hailongwang Company's name. The day after signing this Agreement, Hailongwang Company paid RMB 60 million to Sanlian Company through a bank transfer.

On December 31, 1998, the Office of the Pearl River Qiaodu Preparatory Committee issued the "Meeting Minutes of the Pearl River Qiaodu Preparatory Committee," agreeing that Hailongwang Company and Nanhuaxi would form an investment group to also participate in the 50% investment of the Pearl River Qiaodu project, and to prepare a capital credit certificate of RMB 500 million to participate in cooperation negotiations. The minutes clearly stated: If Pearl River Company withdrew, the investment group composed of Hailongwang Company and Nanhuaxi could appropriately inject capital to maintain the normal progress of the project. Sanlian Company could find another partner to maintain a multi-party cooperation situation. It was hoped that Pearl River Company would continue to participate in the cooperation and retain a 50% investment right.

On July 29, 1999, the defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission issued Notice No. 143 to the Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office, stating: Given that on December 30, 1993, our commission approved the establishment of Qiaofeng Company by Sanlian Company and Jiayu Company through Suiwai Jingmaoye [1993] No. 904, and agreed that Qiaofeng Company could develop, construct, sell, lease, and manage self-built commercial housing on the 654,107 square meter plot approved for use by the Municipal Planning Bureau in documents [92] Chengdipizi No. 39 and No. 55. Given that on July 16, 1997, the Hong Kong court issued a winding-up order against Jiayu Company. According to Hong Kong law, Jiayu Company has no right to dispose of its property. Therefore, the agreements and contracts derived from this have lost their legal basis. Upon deliberation, our commission revokes our Approvals No. 337, No. 6, and No. 9. Upon receipt of this document, please notify the enterprise to return the approval certificate of Pearl River Qiaodu Company and go through the relevant cancellation procedures with the relevant departments. The Pearl River Qiaodu project is an important construction project in our city, and a preparatory committee has long been established. Several matters were clarified at the meeting of the Pearl River Qiaodu Preparatory Committee on December 29 of last year. It is hoped that Sanlian Company can further do a good job in all aspects in accordance with the municipal government's requirements to ensure that the project can smoothly advance in accordance with the law. On October 25 of the same year, the defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission issued Notice No. 233 to the Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office, which read in full: "Our commission issued Suiwai Jingmaoye [1999] No. 143, 'Notice on Revoking Three Approval Documents of Our Commission' on July 29, 1999. Upon deliberation, it is hereby revoked."

**Opinion of the Guangdong High People's Court:**

Article 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a citizen, a legal person, or any other organization considers that his or its lawful rights and interests have been infringed upon by a specific administrative act of an administrative organ or the personnel of an administrative organ, he or it shall have the right to bring a suit before a People's Court in accordance with this Law." Article 41, item (3) provides that a lawsuit shall have specific claims and factual basis.

Article 12 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "If a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has a legal interest in a specific administrative act refuses to accept the act, it may file an administrative lawsuit in accordance with the law."

The Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission is the authority responsible for examining and approving and supervising Sino-foreign cooperative joint ventures in the Guangzhou Municipal People's Government. Although Notice No. 233 was issued as an internal document directly sent to the Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office and copied to Sanlian Company, Pearl River Company, and other relevant units and enterprises, the content of the notice relates to the legal validity of the defendant's previously issued Notice No. 143 and Approvals No. 337, No. 6, and No. 9, and also directly involves the management rights of relevant parties concerning the Pearl River Qiaodu project. This clearly contains rights and obligations under administrative law and creates a new administrative legal relationship. For the relevant parties to the administrative relationship, Notice No. 233 should be considered a reviewable specific administrative act.

Notice No. 233, as well as the related Notice No. 143 and Approvals No. 337, No. 6, and No. 9, are all administrative examination and approval acts performed by the Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission within its authority concerning the establishment, modification, or revocation of specific Sino-foreign cooperative enterprises. The administrative legal relationships arising from these acts should be limited to a specific scope, namely, the Chinese and foreign enterprises that directly participated in the cooperative development of the Guangzhou Pearl River Qiaodu project in accordance with legal procedures. The Pearl River Qiaodu project is a cooperative development project. Any enterprise that participates in the investment and development of the project must join Qiaodu Company, which has the nature of a Sino-foreign cooperative joint venture, in accordance with legal procedures and participate in the investment and cooperation as a shareholder of Qiaodu Company. Article 5 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Ventures provides: "The application for the establishment of a cooperative joint venture shall be submitted, together with the agreements, contracts and articles of association signed between the Chinese and foreign parties, to the department of foreign economic relations and trade under the State Council or to the department or local government authorized by the State Council (hereinafter referred to as the examination and approval authorities) for examination and approval." Article 10 provides: "If a Chinese or foreign party assigns all or part of its rights and obligations under the cooperative joint venture contract, it must obtain the consent of the other party or parties and report to the examination and approval authorities for approval." Since Hailongwang Company did not sign a cooperation contract and articles of association with the various cooperating parties of the Pearl River Qiaodu project, nor did it join the Pearl River Qiaodu project company through approval in accordance with legal procedures, it does not possess investment development rights in the Pearl River Qiaodu project. Therefore, the examination and approval actions taken by the Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission concerning the cooperative development of the Pearl River Qiaodu project did not form an administrative legal relationship with Hailongwang Company.

The relevant agreement signed between the plaintiff, Hailongwang Company, and the third party, Sanlian Company, represents an intention of the two parties to participate in the cooperative operation of the Pearl River Qiaodu project. Moreover, the two parties made corresponding stipulations for different scenarios regarding whether they could ultimately participate in the cooperative operation of the project. Although this agreement was partially performed, with the plaintiff Hailongwang Company paying RMB 60 million to Sanlian Company for investment in the project, whether the plaintiff can obtain the investment development right for the cooperative development of the project depends not solely on the intention of Sanlian Company. The RMB 60 million paid by Hailongwang Company to Sanlian Company only proves that a civil legal relationship was formed between Hailongwang Company and Sanlian Company and cannot serve as a basis for having already obtained the investment development right for the cooperative development of the project.

The Pearl River Qiaodu Preparatory Committee is a temporary organization established by Guangzhou City to strengthen macroeconomic management of the cooperative project. This organization is not an administrative organ at any level, nor is it the competent authority for Sino-foreign cooperative enterprises as defined by law. The nature of this organization determines that any decision it makes can only be advisory or guiding in nature and does not have administrative legal effect. The minutes of the meeting issued by the Office of the Preparatory Committee on December 31, 1998, based on the work meeting of the Preparatory Committee, stating agreement for Hailongwang Company to participate in the project, represent the organization's non-binding opinions regarding related work, not an administrative decision of the government, and have no coercive force over the relevant parties. Hailongwang Company's reliance on these meeting minutes as an administrative decision of the competent government department to confirm its ownership of a 50% development right in the project lacks a factual and legal basis.

In summary, for the plaintiff Hailongwang Company to claim that the defendant's Notice No. 233 infringed upon its lawful rights and interests and file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court, it must prove that it has a legal interest in the notice. Although the challenged Notice No. 233 is a specific administrative act, there is no basis to conclude that the plaintiff Hailongwang Company has a legal interest in this specific administrative act. Therefore, Hailongwang Company does not have standing to sue as the plaintiff in this case, and its lawsuit does not meet the statutory conditions. Following deliberation by the Adjudication Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court, it is hereby ruled as follows:

The lawsuit filed by the plaintiff, Guangzhou Hailongwang Investment Development Co., Ltd., is dismissed.

Court acceptance fee for this case: RMB 100, to be borne by the plaintiff.

After the first-instance judgment, the plaintiff Hailongwang Company refused to accept it and filed an appeal. The defendant Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission expressed agreement with the first-instance court's judgment. The third parties in this case — Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Office, Sanlian Company, Pearl River Company, Qiaodu Company, and Guangda Company — all expressed agreement with the first-instance court's judgment.

**Appellant Hailongwang Company alleged:** The Preparatory Committee for the Pearl River Qiaodu Project was an ad hoc institution established by the government, and its actions should produce administrative legal consequences. Notice No. 143 of the Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission lawfully revoked Qiaodu Company, thereby granting our company the right to engage in cooperation negotiations with Zhujiang Company on the basis of equal competition, each holding a 50% investment right. However, after Notice No. 233 of the Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission revoked Notice No. 143, it objectively deprived our company of the possibility to participate in the competition and infringed upon our company's right to equal competition in investment. We request the revocation of the first-instance ruling.

**Appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission argued:** The agreement between Hailongwang Company and one of the project's investors has no legal connection with the administrative approval act of the Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission. The true reason Hailongwang Company did not obtain a legitimate investment right was not administrative obstruction, but rather its failure to ultimately reach cooperation with the existing shareholders. Notice No. 233 has no legal interest relationship with Hailongwang Company and did not infringe upon its right to fair competition.

**Third Party at First Instance, Guangzhou Overseas Chinese Affairs Office argued:** Hailongwang Company did not obtain a legitimate investment qualification in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project, nor did it actually engage in equal competition in the project. It has no proprietary interest in the project. The Preparatory Committee for the Pearl River Qiaodu Project did not grant Hailongwang Company the right to invest in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project.

**Third Party at First Instance, Sanlian Company argued:** Hailongwang Company did not meet the subject qualification requirements or the time conditions for participating in the competition. Hailongwang Company's payment of RMB 60,000,000 to our company does not mean it enjoys proprietary interests in the cooperative project. Qiaodu Company is a lawfully established company that has always existed legally. Hailongwang Company's view that Notice No. 233 "revived" an "illegal" Qiaodu Company, thereby affecting Hailongwang Company's interests, is erroneous.

**Third Party at First Instance, Zhujiang Company argued:** The development and operation rights for the Pearl River Qiaodu Project were established long before Hailongwang Company was founded. Hailongwang Company never invested in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project. The "investment" referred to by Hailongwang Company was merely an agreement between it and Sanlian Company. Notice No. 233 only concerns Qiaodu Company and Qiaofeng Company and their shareholders, and did not infringe upon Hailongwang Company's right to equal competition.

**Third Party at First Instance, Qiaodu Company argued:** Hailongwang Company does not have a legitimate investment subject qualification in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project, does not have the right to equal competition in the project, and has no proprietary interests. The reason Hailongwang Company's investment was blocked was not Notice No. 233, but rather Hailongwang Company's lack of capacity to invest in the project. The summary of the Preparatory Committee meeting constitutes an administrative guidance act, not an administrative decision, and has no legal effect. Qiaodu Company is a lawfully established company, and its legality is beyond doubt. Hailongwang Company cannot prove, based on civil legal acts and administrative guidance acts, that it has a legal interest relationship with Notice No. 233.

**Third Party at First Instance, Guangda Company argued:** Hailongwang Company's assertion that Notice No. 233 infringed upon its right to equal competition lacks factual and legal basis. Guangda Company, as a foreign investor, is entitled to the protection of its investments and legitimate rights and interests within the territory of China.

Upon trial, the Supreme People's Court confirmed that the facts found by the Guangdong High People's Court in its first-instance judgment were true.

**The Supreme People's Court holds:**

Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "In any of the following circumstances, a citizen, legal person, or other organization may initiate an administrative lawsuit in accordance with law: (1) the specific administrative act complained of involves its neighboring rights or right to fair competition; (2) there is a legal interest relationship with the administrative reconsideration decision complained of, or it was added as a third party in the reconsideration proceedings; (3) it requests the competent administrative authority to pursue the liability of the tortfeasor in accordance with law; (4) there is a legal interest relationship with the revocation or modification of a specific administrative act." Appellant Hailongwang Company, based on the agreement signed with Sanlian Company, paid RMB 60,000,000 to Sanlian Company as an investment in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project, resulting in partial performance of the agreement. However, Sanlian Company was only one of the three parties investing in Qiaodu Company and had no authority to decide that Hailongwang Company could participate in the development of the Pearl River Qiaodu Project. The relationship formed between Hailongwang Company and Sanlian Company was merely a civil legal relationship, which cannot prove that Hailongwang Company held shares in Qiaodu Company. Since Hailongwang Company did not sign a cooperation contract or articles of association with the parties of the Pearl River Qiaodu Project, nor did it join Qiaodu Company after examination and approval in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Ventures, Hailongwang Company's ground of appeal that Notice No. 233, issued by the appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission concerning Qiaodu Company, has a legal interest relationship with it, is untenable.

The Preparatory Committee for the Pearl River Qiaodu Project was a guidance and coordination body established pursuant to the "Resolution of the Standing Committee of the Guangzhou Municipal People's Congress on Deliberating the Implementation Plan of Motion No. 42 of the Third Session of the Ninth Guangzhou Municipal People's Congress Submitted by the Municipal People's Government." This resolution provides a clear explanation of the nature and functions of the Preparatory Committee. There is no administrative subordination relationship between the Preparatory Committee and the appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission. The summary of the Preparatory Committee meeting is merely administrative guidance in nature and is not compulsory. The statement in the summary regarding "agreeing to Hailongwang Company's participation in the investment in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project" cannot alter the legal status of the parties in Qiaodu Company. Only by negotiating with the parties of the Pearl River Qiaodu Company and being approved by the competent authority in accordance with statutory procedures to become a shareholder of Qiaodu Company could Hailongwang Company obtain the right to invest and develop the Pearl River Qiaodu Project. The meeting summary concerning the Pearl River Qiaodu Project cannot legally create new rights and obligations and has no administrative legal effect. Appellant Hailongwang Company's ground of appeal that the work summary of the Preparatory Committee and Notice No. 233 of the appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission formed a legal interest relationship with it, is untenable.

Qiaodu Company is a project company for the development and construction of the Pearl River Qiaodu real estate. The administrative approvals made by the appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission concerning Qiaodu Company within its authority did not legally exclude or restrict Appellant Hailongwang Company's right to obtain investment in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project. During the period from the issuance of Notice No. 143 by the appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission to the issuance of Notice No. 233, the equity structure of Qiaodu Company never changed, and the nature of the legal relationship between Hailongwang Company and the other investors in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project also did not change because Hailongwang Company did not obtain the qualification to invest in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project. The right to fair competition protected by law is the right of equal subjects to obtain legitimate interests based on the same rights and obligations. The fair competition relationship protected by law is a legitimate competitive relationship between equal subjects under the same rights and obligations. Since there is no corresponding relationship of rights and obligations between Appellant Hailongwang Company and the other investors in the Pearl River Qiaodu Project, the right of competition it claims is not a right to fair competition under the law. Appellant Hailongwang Company's ground of appeal that Notice No. 233 of the appellee Guangzhou Foreign Economic Commission infringed upon its right to fair competition is untenable.

In summary, Hailongwang Company's initiation of this administrative lawsuit lacks factual basis. The first-instance ruling found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. After deliberation by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 41, Item (3) and Article 61, Item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ordered as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original ruling is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by Appellant Hailongwang Company.
